current_static_findings.evidence: PROBE_OPERATION_ACK_V2_ENABLED defaults true and creates producers plus starts dispatcher before consumer readiness receipts exist
current_static_findings.consequence: a deployment can publish commands and lifecycle events before downstream authority is proven ready

current_static_findings.evidence: ACK is published and the Redis command is deleted by operation ID without comparing stored command revision to ACK revision
current_static_findings.consequence: a wrong-revision ACK can delete the correct pending command after a broker ACK

current_static_findings.evidence: stale detection compares only the maximum completed revision instead of the maximum authoritative desired revision
current_static_findings.consequence: an older ACK can advance after a newer desired operation exists but has not completed

current_static_findings.evidence: Kafka success precedes the PostgreSQL published transition and no broker receipt is durably recorded
current_static_findings.consequence: a crash or commit failure after ACK republishes the same event at a new Kafka offset with no explicit outcome-unknown receipt

current_static_findings.evidence: duplicate acceptance requires the original Kafka partition and offset to match exactly
current_static_findings.consequence: a legal redelivery of the same event and payload at a new offset is rejected as an identity collision

current_static_findings.evidence: an empty ProducerConfig.IdempotentKey selects RoundRobin even when Send carries a nonempty message key
current_static_findings.consequence: commands and ACKs for one tenant and probe can move partitions and lose per-key ordering

current_static_findings.evidence: the command consumer passes only message.Value so Route cannot validate Kafka key headers partition offset or schema rail
current_static_findings.consequence: a body-valid command can enter Redis despite envelope mismatch and no source receipt can be retained

current_static_findings.evidence: the ACK message contract omits key and command_revision header checks while its consumer enables DLQ commit without DLQPermanentOnly
current_static_findings.consequence: wrong-key or transient database failures can be quarantined and committed instead of redelivered to authority

current_static_findings.evidence: an idempotency-key conflict returns the old operation without comparing the canonical request hash operation type or probe
current_static_findings.consequence: same key with a different command can be reported as a successful replay

current_static_findings.evidence: duplicate detection checks only that a receipt exists for operation_id and does not compare source event ID or canonical payload hash
current_static_findings.consequence: a conflicting later ACK can be silently accepted as the original receipt

current_static_findings.evidence: Redis uses one hash-wide TTL and List returns the oldest twenty revisions without filtering command expiry
current_static_findings.consequence: expired commands can be delivered while newer commands are starved behind stale entries

current_static_findings.evidence: expiry updates operation and history outside a transaction that also creates the lifecycle outbox event
current_static_findings.consequence: PostgreSQL authority can say expired without an immutable event for consumers and reconcile

current_static_findings.evidence: every completed operation writes reported_config_version and reported_config_hash regardless of operation type
current_static_findings.consequence: connectivity certificate restart or batch operations can overwrite configuration reported state
